title: One Quick Game Tonight
situation: A friend texts asking if you want to hop on for a quick game tonight.
tip: Casual invites get casual answers. React first (콜/좋아), then add a quick logistics question to keep it moving instead of just saying yes.

turns.ko: 야 오늘 저녁에 게임 한판 콜?
turns.en: Yo, you down for a quick game tonight?

turns.prompt: Say yes casually and ask when

choices.en: Down, down — around what time?
choices.feedback: Quick reaction (콜콜) plus a follow-up question — exactly how friends lock in plans over text.

choices.en: Yes, sounds good. I will join.
choices.feedback: Way too formal — sounds like replying to a boss, not a friend texting about games.

choices.en: Down for a quick game tonight?
choices.feedback: You just repeated their question back — that doesn't answer or move the chat forward.

turns.ko: 9시 어때? 나 밥 먹고 바로 켤게
turns.en: How about 9? I'll hop on right after dinner.

turns.prompt: Agree and ask what you're playing

choices.ko: 좋아 9시 ㄱㄱ 오늘 뭐 할 건데?
choices.en: Cool, 9 it is — what are we playing today?
choices.feedback: Confirms the time and naturally asks the next thing (the game). Keeps the plan rolling.

choices.en: It is possible for me to participate at 9.
choices.feedback: Stiff and robotic — no friend texts in full 존댓말 sentences about gaming.

choices.ko: 아 나 사실 게임 잘 안 해
choices.en: Ah, I don't really play games actually.
choices.feedback: Contradicts the whole vibe — you just agreed to play, so this kills the plan.

turns.en: LoL? Or just a round of PUBG?

choices.ko: 배그 ㄱ 요즘 롤 하면 너무 빡쳐 ㅋㅋ
choices.en: PUBG, let's go — LoL gets me way too tilted these days lol
choices.feedback: Makes a choice and drops a relatable reaction with ㅋㅋ — totally how friends text about games.

choices.ko: 둘 다 제가 잘 모르는 게임입니다.
choices.en: Both are games I am not familiar with.
choices.feedback: Too formal and oddly distant — doesn't pick or react like a friend would.

choices.en: LoL? Or a round of PUBG?
choices.feedback: You bounced the same question back instead of choosing — leaves them hanging.

turns.ko: ㅋㅋㅋ ㅇㅋ 그럼 배그로 ㄱㄱ 이따 봐
turns.en: Lolol ok, PUBG it is — see you later.

choices.ko: ㅇㅋㅇㅋ 이따 봐 9시 늦지 마라 ㅋㅋ
choices.en: Kk, see you later — don't be late at 9 lol
choices.feedback: Natural sign-off with a playful jab — friends love teasing on the way out.

choices.en: Then I shall see you later.
choices.feedback: Far too formal for closing a casual game plan with a buddy.

choices.en: By the way, what are you doing this weekend?
choices.feedback: Random subject change right at the goodbye — the chat was already wrapping up.

title: Weekend Climbing Plan
situation: A friend texts to invite you to an indoor climbing gym this weekend.
tip: When a friend proposes a weekend activity, show interest with a reaction (오 좋다/콜) and ask a practical follow-up (when/where/what to bring) so it turns into a real plan.

turns.prompt: React with interest and ask which day

choices.en: Oh nice — Saturday or Sunday?
choices.feedback: Warm reaction plus a practical follow-up — this is how a casual invite becomes a real plan.

choices.en: I agree to going climbing this weekend.
choices.feedback: Sounds like signing a contract — nobody texts a friend in this register.

choices.en: Is the weather nice this weekend?
choices.feedback: Just echoes their info instead of answering — doesn't move toward a plan.

turns.ko: 토욜 오전 어때? 사람 적을 때 가자
turns.en: Saturday morning? Let's go when it's less crowded.

turns.prompt: Agree but admit you're a beginner

choices.ko: 콜 근데 나 완전 초보인데 괜찮아?
choices.en: Down — but I'm a total beginner, is that ok?
choices.feedback: Agrees and honestly checks in with a question — keeps it real and keeps them talking.

choices.ko: 저는 클라이밍 경험이 전혀 없는 초보자입니다.
choices.en: I am a beginner with no climbing experience whatsoever.
choices.feedback: The meaning's fine but the 존댓말 is too stiff for texting a friend.

choices.ko: 토욜 오전 어때 사람 적을 때?
choices.en: Saturday morning, when it's less crowded?
choices.feedback: You repeated their suggestion back word for word — that's not a reply.

turns.ko: ㄱㅊㄱㅊ 내가 다 알려줄게 신발만 빌리면 돼
turns.en: All good, I'll show you everything — you just need to rent shoes.

turns.prompt: Show relief and ask what to bring

choices.ko: 오 다행 ㅋㅋ 그럼 뭐 챙겨가면 돼?
choices.en: Oh phew lol — so what should I bring?
choices.feedback: Relieved reaction plus a useful question — exactly the kind of follow-up that keeps planning natural.

choices.en: I would appreciate it if you could inform me of what to prepare.
choices.feedback: Email-level politeness — totally mismatched with a casual climbing text.

choices.ko: 나 클라이밍 말고 등산이 더 좋은데
choices.en: I'd actually rather go hiking than climbing.
choices.feedback: You already agreed to climbing — flipping the plan now is off and confusing.

turns.ko: 편한 운동복이랑 물만 챙겨와 끝나고 밥 ㄱ
turns.en: Just bring comfy workout clothes and water — food after, let's go.

choices.en: Down — so excited, see you Saturday!
choices.feedback: Locks the plan with genuine excitement — a perfect upbeat close for a friend.

choices.en: I shall proceed accordingly.
choices.feedback: Sounds like a work confirmation, not a friend hyped about the weekend.

choices.en: So who's paying for the food?
choices.feedback: Oddly transactional right at the close — friends just say 끝나고 같이 먹자 and sort it later.

title: Picking Up a New Hobby
situation: You bump into a friend who just started a new hobby, and you're curious to hear about it.
tip: Curiosity carries the conversation. Pile on follow-up questions (진짜?/어땠어?/얼마나 했어?) and react warmly so your friend keeps sharing about their new thing.

turns.en: So I started baking recently, you know.

turns.prompt: React with surprise and ask why baking

choices.en: Whoa, really? Why baking all of a sudden?
choices.feedback: Surprise reaction (헐 진짜?) plus a 되묻기 question — this is exactly how you make a friend open up.

choices.en: I am surprised to hear you started baking.
choices.feedback: The 존댓말 makes it sound distant — friends in person react with 헐/진짜, not full polite sentences.

choices.ko: 아 그래. 나도 밥 먹어야 되는데.
choices.en: Oh ok. I should eat something too.
choices.feedback: Ignores what they shared and changes the subject — kills their excitement.

turns.ko: 그냥 스트레스 풀려고? 빵 만들면 좀 힐링되더라고
turns.en: Just to de-stress, I guess? Making bread is kinda therapeutic.

turns.prompt: Relate and ask how long they've done it

choices.ko: 오, 그럴 것 같아. 근데 시작한 지 얼마나 됐어?
choices.en: Oh, I can see that. How long have you been doing it?
choices.feedback: Validates them and asks another follow-up — keeps the curiosity flowing naturally.

choices.ko: 베이킹의 치유 효과에 대해 동의하는 바입니다.
choices.en: I concur regarding the therapeutic effects of baking.
choices.feedback: Absurdly formal for chatting face to face with a friend.

choices.en: So when are you giving me bread?
choices.feedback: Jumps to demanding bread — it shifts focus off their story too soon and feels self-centered.

turns.ko: 한두 달? 처음엔 진짜 다 망했는데 요즘 좀 늘었어
turns.en: Like two months? At first everything flopped, but I've gotten better lately.

turns.prompt: Encourage and ask what they made recently

choices.en: That's awesome, I'm jealous — what'd you make recently?
choices.feedback: Warm hype (대박/부럽다) plus a follow-up — perfect for keeping a friend sharing.

choices.en: I presume it is the result of continuous effort.
choices.feedback: Reads like a written report — no one talks to a friend like this.

choices.en: Two months means you're still a beginner, huh.
choices.feedback: Slightly dismissive — it deflates their progress instead of cheering them on.

turns.ko: 지난주에 휘낭시에 구웠는데 그건 좀 성공했어 ㅋㅋ
turns.en: I baked financiers last week and those actually turned out lol

turns.prompt: Hint that you want to try one

choices.ko: 오, 휘낭시에 ㅋㅋ 다음에 나도 하나 맛봐도 돼?
choices.en: Oh, financiers lol. Can I try one next time?
choices.feedback: Playful and hints at next time — a natural, friendly way to wrap while leaving the door open.

choices.ko: 다음 기회에 시식할 수 있도록 부탁드립니다.
choices.en: I request the opportunity to taste them next time.
choices.feedback: Over-the-top polite — clashes hard with the easy ㅋㅋ tone of the chat.

choices.en: What's a financier? I'm not interested.
choices.feedback: Saying you're not interested shuts the whole conversation down after they opened up.
